title: RAW_UNSCREENED: source and recipient condition jointly reverse treatment sign
summary: Complete VII, XIX, and XXXIII entries contrast harm/help by bath identity and recipient condition: VII harms hydrops, XIX harms healthy recipients but helps diseased bodies, and XXXIII helps hydrops.

design.mechanism: Outcome sign is jointly conditioned by source identity and recipient condition, rather than fixed by one body-term family.
source_clauses_exact: Sed nocet ydropicis, cum sit dulcissima potu:
Vim consumendi non habet, unde nocet
Culma nocet sanis, morbida membra iuuat.
design.whole_reading: A complete paragraph would let source identity and recipient condition jointly select a signed outcome, retaining VII versus XXXIII hydrops contrast and XIX healthy/sick contrast.
design.nearest_rival: Uniform body-effect model assigning one stable sign to hydrops or healthy/sick status across entries.
design.distinguishing_observation: Require a stable source-by-recipient relation that permits sign reversal only when the source or explicit condition changes.
design.strongest_likely_failure: Entries are independent bath claims with no reusable recipient relation, making the signed graph overstructured.
assumption_costs: Source identity remains available in the whole record.
Recipient conditions scope over the stated outcome.
No target term or medical efficacy is inferred.
design.scope_note: Source-only raw proposal; polarity is a source-clause relation, not a target meaning.
